analysis.title: US Market Intelligence - Afternoon Briefing (Nov 24, 2026)
key_insights: JPM US Market Intel moves back to a Tactically Cautious view. The bear case played out last week and the desk admits it missed the tactical bullish call, having relied on NVDA and capital markets as support for a Tech bottom.

A tactical bounce is seen as likely after the aggressive selloff, but the desk does not expect a sustainable rally or a near-term bottom. 2018 is cited as the best historical comp, where the late-year bounce was faded.
Desk expects further rotation away from Tech, with Tech trades getting increasingly crowded, adding pain risk if a tactical bounce comes.

Conditions to flip bullish: positioning reset, cyclicals outperforming defensives or a selloff in recession/stagflation baskets, lower vol, time to digest news and a new earnings season in mid-Jan. A Fed pause in December to go in Jan/Mar is a positive tail risk.
Market closed mixed: SPX -0.5%, NDX -2.0%, RTY +0.6%, SPW +0.5%. Mag 7 fell 1.7% with NVDA -5.9%, semis -8.6%, hardware -6.5%, AI data centers and power -4.0%. Software outperformed semis by 8.9%.
Factor moves: Cyclicals vs Defensives -5.8%, Value L/S +3.0%, Recession L/S +1.2%, PURE Quality +0.3%. The recession trade is leading again.

Tariffs: WSJ reports the US is preparing new Section 301 tariffs following the excess-capacity probe of 16 economies. Rate and scope are unknown. JPM's Aziz expects the average effective rate to return toward the pre-IEEPA level of 13.8% vs 11.2% in November 2026.

Pending Section 232 and other tariff actions include furniture and cabinets rising on Jan 1 2027, Canadian autos, trucks, parts and steel at 50% from Jan 1 2027 absent a deal, and polysilicon derivatives on Dec 4. Wind turbines, robotics and industrial machinery are in a negotiation window to April 20, 2027.

Section 301 tariffs face legal challenges and the USCIT may rule before YE26. Courts have read tariff power as belonging to Congress, so either set could be struck down, but resolution may run well into 2027. A Dem-majority Congress would need material Republican support to override.

NVDA: Huang's reinstatement removes the leadership question, but the desk flags lawmaker pushback, a Dec 3 Senate Banking testimony, open SEC and California AG investigations, and pending chip-control bills (MATCH Act, Remote Access Security Act). Ron Adler says governance and political uncertainty should weigh on equity multiples.

Semis desk color: concern that 2028 numbers are too high and need cuts to reset the bar. HPE flagged that pricing increases will moderate next year. The Frontier LAB IPO breaking hurt sentiment, and the desk was much better for sale across the complex.

ETF desk: real money demand in SOXX and growth ETFs was offset by supply in MAGS. The desk is better to sell today, with best calls in VWO, VNQ and VTI. EM AI picks-and-shovels demand returned in Taiwan (EWT, FLTW) and Korea (EWY, FLKR).

Healthcare desk: the INSM deal adds to the sector bid, which looks cover-driven. Biotech has more long-only action. Tools and diagnostics see trims in TWST and DHR, shorts press in ZBH and GMED, LO demand in GILD, shorts in PFE, HF demand in HUM.
JPM Research 2027 SPX target is 8,200 (~13% upside), assuming about 17% y/y EPS growth to $430 and a P/E re-rating from about 17x to about 19x.

Fundamentals: 26Q3 SPX median earnings growth was about 12% vs the 10-year average of 12.6% per FactSet, and median profit margins hit fresh all-time highs. The desk says AI risks are tied to financing and the consumption wealth effect rather than capex.

market_movers.rationale: Fell 5.9% after adding back 33% on Huang's return. Lawmaker pushback, SEC and California investigations, and a Dec 3 Senate testimony remain overhangs.
The Insmed-Sanofi deal lifted pharma and healthcare names on the day.
An 8-K stoked M&A hopes in SMID Internet, with lateral strength in SNAP and CPNG.
HPE flagged that pricing increases will moderate next year, weighing on semis sentiment.

sector_views.rationale: Tactically cautious. Uncertainty around NVDA and peers and opacity on 2028 make Tech longs highly uncertain near term, though Mag 7 and security software are the safest areas.
Squeeze risk exists, so use options to play a rebound. Desk flow is heavily for sale.
The bid is seen as cover-driven, with two-way flow in biotech.
UK and EU likely to outperform, especially if the dollar sees profit-taking.

earnings_insights: Reporting 11/24: DELL, ADI, ADSK, BBY, WDAY, HPQ and others. Tomorrow (11/25): CLSK, DE.
Upcoming tech earnings: CRWD (Dec 1), MRVL (Dec 1), CRM (Dec 2), AVGO (Dec 9), ORCL (Dec 10), MU (Dec 17).
26Q3 SPX median earnings growth was about 12% (reported, per FactSet) vs the 10-year average EPS growth of 12.6%.
JPM 2027 outlook assumes EPS of $430, about 17% y/y growth (forecast).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Treasuries rallied, led by the 5-year (-2.7bp). The 10Y fell 1.4bp.
JPM's Aziz expects new tariffs to restore the pre-IEEPA level.
Hiking-cycle uncertainty is a headwind. A pause would be a positive tail.
The path after December is uncertain.

tension_points.bull_case: Aggressive selloff and oversold conditions make a tactical bounce likely. NVDA and capital markets could support a Tech bottom.
tension_points.bear_case: Uncertainty in Tech fundamentals, 2028 numbers too high, a hawkish Fed narrative and crowded trades mean a bounce may be faded as in 2018.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Positioning reset, cyclicals outperforming defensives, lower vol, or a Fed pause in December would flip the desk bullish.
